column3: The Hebrew repeats the Philistines as those fled from and has no separate word for “many” among the slain. BSB uses “them” and supplies “many.”
The Hebrew repeats the Philistines as those striking Saul’s sons; BSB uses “they.”
The Hebrew says the archers found him, repeating the archers in describing his suffering; BSB uses “overtook him” and leaves the repeated archers implicit.
The Hebrew says Saul took “the sword”; BSB specifies “his own sword.”
The Hebrew says “the men of Israel” fled and that the Philistines dwelt in the abandoned cities. BSB uses “the army of Israel” and “occupied their cities.”
The Hebrew leaves Saul unnamed and the people sent unnamed; BSB supplies Saul and “messengers.” It has singular “the house of their idols,” rendered plural “the temples of their idols.”
The Hebrew says they fastened his body to the wall; BSB uses “hung his body.”
